In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of activation of the extrinsic pathway by VIIa and TF.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ca2+-binding properties of factor VIIa and its interaction with TF are complex, and the Ca2+-induced conformational changes that occur in factor VIIa and TF are important for the development of catalytic activity.
Ca2+ binding to factor VIIa enhances its interaction with TF and development of catalytic activity.

Ca2+ binding to the protease domain of factor VIIa is a prerequisite for its functional interaction with TF and that this binding site may play a key role in the development of catalytic activity of factor VIIa·Ca·TF complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Ca2+-induced conformational change in the protease domain of factor VIIa is essential for development of catalytic activity and for interaction with TF.
the protease Ca2+-binding domain is essential for the interaction of factor VIIa with TF and for the development of catalytic activity.
the Ca2+-binding domain of factor VIIa enhances the catalytic activity of VIIa by increasing the functional affinity of VIIa for TF and the rate of factor X activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
factor VIIa·TF binding is enhanced ∼105-fold by Ca2+ binding in the serine proteases domain of factor VIIa.

Ca2+ binding to factor VIIa, and probably to other serine and metalloproteases, is not a simple on/off process, but rather is highly dependent on the local ionic environment and the presence of other proteins.
the Ca2+-binding properties of VIIa and the Ca2+-dependent interaction with TF can play a role in the activation of the coagulation protease cascade and the initiation of the extrinsic pathway.
